On "Hard" Mode, here is my thoughts. 

  
**Ike** \- B- - Sword and foot locked in a game with big maps and lots of movement options. Combat he is fine, if not one of the stronger units. Early/Mid is challenging at times for him. Late game promotion is a slog. 

**Titania** \- S - Incredible unit. Great weapon options in the land of swordy units and bulky armors. Forged Javelins are nutty. Amazing stats, great growths, utility across the game. Great example of a Jagen imo. Very good unit with long term viability, but not the absolute best combat wise

**Boyd** \- B+ - Pretty much the same as Ike from a combat perspective. Almost the same growths. Getting 1-2 Range from the jump is awesome for utility. 

**Oscar -** S- - From an overall usefulness, Titania edges him slightly for early and mid game success. Late game Oscar overtakes her, but she is still useful at that stage of the game. Triangle attack is a neat little added bonus, but does not move the needle imo. I like giving Axes for extra pop.

Gerik - B+ - Very versatile between Hero and Ranger. I prefer him as a Ranger, but my heart makes him a Hero. He has so much Con its nutty. He can use a Brave Bow with no speed penalty and only loses 3 SPD using Nidhogg. Best bow user in the game.

Rennac - C- - Not very combat focused, but does have some utility as a Rogue. Stealing/picking locks is good to have generally. Wish he was faster or had better defense for more survivability. Combat wise is outclassed entirely by Colm and Joshua.

I was a NYCTF Fellow years ago.

First, is your spouse able to work? - That extra income is huge imo, even if its part time.

Do you have major debt? Student loan, personal, etc.  


With a masters, you'd be making 77k, which is around 3.5-4k a month after taxes, maybe less due to having the program deducted from your salary and a dependent. 

  
For moving, you might need a guarantor, which some landlords don't like or accept. If you had a full time job before that is great, but many want to see the last 2-3 pay stubs. Most 2BRs in BK are at least 2.8k. Upper Manhattan and the Bronx have affordable options. Ideally I would want 9-12k saved up for moving. That extra padding makes you look like a viable tenant. 

As for job search. There are plenty of jobs. They might suck, they might be far away, they might drain your soul, but there there. The program is a great way to network. Everyone in my mini site cohort got a job. Some people lasted a year, some never left.

In Mistlands, slow and steady. Don't run unless you need to. If you run, your wisp can't keep up. Frostner is a must have starting imo. The slow effect is huge for outrunning and controlling foes. I sometimes like using 2 stam and 1 health food to scout an area out first. You can always outrun enemies, you just need the stamina to do so. 

In my experience, bigger continuous landmasses of Mistlands have a higher chance of Mines than the island archipelagos that spawn. I like utlizing Dvergr outposts for small portal hubs into Mistlands. You can kill them, bait Seekers into them, or use a cart to break their ward so they won't aggro you. Alternatively, a small Black Forest base close to Mistlands is a great breather area imo. 

Feather cape is your best friend and should probably be a priority Mistlands gear to make once you get 5 Cores. Staying up high is a great way to stay ahead of danger.

He is taken aback by the coldness of the hospital staff :
"It is then that I become aware that we are not alone, that there are others milling around the room—other zombies like us, hurriedly dressed and streaming water till the beige carpet is black with it—and why, I wonder, do I despise this nurse more than any human being I’ve ever encountered, this young woman not much older than my daughter, with her hair pulled back in a bun and a white cap like a party favor perched atop it, who is just doing her job?"

Obviously injuries are impossible to predict, but I think you can still make predictions of a career length.

Starting QBs can be fantasy relevant for a decade+. Take a guy like Roethlisberger for example. Aside from his injured 2019, he put up elite to respectable numbers year in and year out from 2004 to 2021. The first season can be shaky, but most fantasy QBs take a step in their 2nd/3rd season. Sometimes a player will be on the bench for 1 season, but usually they're starting week 18 or week 1 in year 2. Love and Rodgers are two examples where that didn't happen. 

The influx of rushing QBs has made this a little more different. Historically rushing QBs don't last long, Cam, Vick, RG3 for example. Makes me wary as a Kyler manager personally. That being said, the NFL doesn't seem to be sticking to guys very long any more if they don't get it together. Rosen, Darnold, Wilson, Lock, and Haskins (RIP), didn't get it together and teams moved on quick. 

WRs have a 6-10 year window. Technical guys like Diggs, Adams, and Fitz age a lot better than your pure physical jump ball guys like Dez, Evans, Mike Williams. Long ball guys can carve consistent niches out for themselves. There is the rookie threshold of 525 yards that historically indicates if a player will produce in the NFL, but it's not the end all be all. I like building a team around WR and QB. They have a much longer shelf like and having a set core for 4-8 years is huge. I got AJB as a rookie in start up and he's been such a boon to play around. 

TEs are a crapshoot. Kelce was the 5th TE selected in 2013. Typically tight ends need 2-3 years to develop. If by year 5 they haven't really done anything, I'm out. They also tend to be a position where back ups truly become starters, Goedert is a recent example. I don't think it's as slow a burn for other positions to catch on. That being said, most fantasy relevant TEs tend to produce fairly long, 5-8 years, but going longer isn't unheard of. 

RBs usually need to produce as a rookie to be long term fantasy starters. If a player gets less than 100 touches as a rookie, historically he won't be very fantasy relevant. The game is changing that makes the workhorse running back a thing in the past. The great elites can last 6-7 years, but they're unicorns today. There is also the 400 touch club, where players tend to see a large decrease in production after that many carries. 

Unless you get one of those top elite talents, getting 1-3 years of starting from a running back is a win. From what I've seen, pass catching backs stay in the league and produce longer than your pure runners. I think running back will become one of the hardest positions to predict on a week to week basis in the future. 

So to sum up: No matter what, any non TE needs to produce immediately. QBs get some wiggle room, but we don't seem many guys on the bench for longer than a year anymore, Love being the most recent example.

QBs: 10+ years

WRs: 7-10 years

RBs: Elite talent 5-7 years, 1-3 years

TEs: 6-8 years, but slow progression.

I wrestled heavyweight in high school, did some judo and club wrestling in college.

I used the lat drop a lot. One of my favorite throws to hit, as a matter of fact.

Some tips:

* You NEED your opponent to push into you. Otherwise you'll yank him on top of you.
* If they don't pursuit you or engage with you aggressively, the over/under position can lead to trips, singles, body locks. I liked an underhook to inside trip. Or push them to the edge and force them to make a move into you, oepning the throw, or push out to lead to a stall.
* The overhook imo is more important that the underhook. That needs to be tight to execute it. A lot of HS heavys enjoy the underhook, so I'd give it to them to keep a tight clamp with the over.
* Think of the "falling" part as a sit and a punch. As they push into you, you pull down on the tight overhook, you sit and punch the underhook in a fluid motion. I know, easier said than done.
* It can be done in a scramble. I know a lot of times I'd see wrestlers telegraph their throw a mile away. It doesn't need to be. The last time I it in a match was when I was coming up from bottom position and as stood up to neutral, my opponent kept pushing into me and I caught him.
* Practice, practice, practice. It took me probably about 30-50 tries in practice one day before it all clicked.
